How to read Model Value

The one idea that matters most in this workbook

Model Value (€) is generated from a player's own performance, age, league strength and minutes — a regression fit once across the whole population. Transfermarkt market values are used only to calibrate the euro scale, never copied. When Model Value sits well above the listed Market Value, the player is flagged as UNDERVALUED. Methodology

How every number on this dashboard is built.

Model Value (€) — metrics in, price out

Model Value is not a copy or rescale of a player's own Transfermarkt market value. It's the output of a single regression fit once across the entire player pool:

ln(Market Value + 1) ~ Composite performance score
   + Age + Age²
   + ln(Minutes played)
   + League Strength (0–100, pyramid position)
   + Position

Market values are used only in aggregate, to teach the model what euro amount the transfer market typically attaches to a given level of output, age, league context and position. Once fit, the coefficients are applied to every player's own metrics — including players with no listed market value — to produce Model Value: what the market should pay for a player with those underlying numbers, independent of what they happen to be priced at today.

Undervalued Ratio = Model Value ÷ Market Value. A ratio well above 1.0 means the player's output/age/league profile is worth more than the market currently prices them at — the definition of undervalued used throughout this dashboard. Players with no market value on file still get a Model Value (useful for lower-league/youth scouting) but no ratio (NO MARKET COMP).

Two performance scores

League-Relative Score
Percentile vs the player's own league/position peers only — reads as "how dominant is he in his current league."
Composite Score
League-Relative Score scaled down by league strength — cross-league comparable, used for Model Value, sorting, and Youth Prospects, so a standout in a weak league isn't confused with a standout in a strong one.

League tiers

Tiers are inherited from a curated football-pyramid table (division position in each country's league system — not derived from market value). Leagues absent from that table get a conservative fallback tier from their division depth so nothing is left unranked.

Peak-age windows

Position-specific windows classify every player as RISING, in their PEAK WINDOW, or PAST PEAK. The flagship "Undervalued & Not Past Peak" board excludes anyone already past their window.

Youth vs. senior

Youth league
The whole competition is youth (Tier 6, or filename-tagged U17/U19/…) — every team in it is Youth.
Youth team
Inside a senior league, reserve/academy sides are flagged by name pattern (…II, …B, U15–U23, Youth, Junior, Academy, Reserves) so first-team recruitment boards aren't diluted by feeder-team stats.

Physical / quick-league fit

Benchmark
Czech First League — a fast, duel-heavy, physically demanding top flight.
Method
Every player's duel/aerial/tempo metrics are z-scored against the Czech First League's own per-position averages (not their own league's). A high score means they already produce Czech-top-flight-level physical/tempo numbers. Goalkeepers are excluded from this board — duel-rate stats are too low-sample and not the relevant style question for them.

Brighton mechanics — buy low, develop, resell

Modelled on Brighton & Hove Albion's own recruitment approach: a wide global scouting net into mid-tier and unfashionable leagues, a strong preference for players still short of their prime, and a willingness to pay for underlying data over reputation — buying early, developing on the pitch, and banking the resale profit once the market catches up.

Brighton Score
30% Age Fit (peaks 19–21) + 30% Composite Score (cross-league quality) + 25% Undervaluation (Value Ratio percentile) + 15% Trajectory (Rising highest, Peak Window partial, Past Peak excluded).
Development Upside (€)
The valuation regression re-run with one change: age swapped for the position's typical peak-age, holding quality/league/minutes fixed — the pure "aging into peak" effect the market already pays for, without speculating about further skill growth.
Prime Target / Strong Fit / Speculative
Brighton Score bands at 75 / 62 / 48, restricted to players age 25 or under who are not yet past their peak window.

Role archetypes

Each position is split into 2-3 statistical playing styles via weighted z-score profiles over the relevant per-90 metrics (e.g. CB → Ball-Playing CB vs Aggressive Stopper) — a specific, recruitable target rather than a bare position label, the way a data-driven scouting department actually briefs a scout.

Squad needs & similar to our squad

Squad Needs
FC Hradec Králové's actual current senior squad (real Wyscout data) benchmarked position-by-position: each position's best player's Composite Score is percentile-ranked against the full cross-league pool at that position. Below the 45th percentile = High priority; below 70th = Medium. Every priority position gets a target list of undervalued, not-past-peak players who outscore the current starter.
Similar to Our Squad
For every current squad player, a cosine-similarity search over position-relevant per-90 metrics finds the closest statistical matches in the full universe — useful for succession planning or finding a cut-price like-for-like.

Club style profiles

Each club's Attacking/Creation/Defending/Pressing/Aerial subscores are percentile-ranked across every rated senior club, producing a 0-100 tactical-identity profile comparable club-to-club. Style Similarity finds the clubs whose profile most closely matches a reference club's by cosine similarity — useful for judging whether an incoming player's style will transfer, or which clubs to study for tactical ideas.

Set-piece specialists

Corner/free-kick delivery, aerial threat, and shot/box-presence metrics are z-scored and blended into six set-piece roles (Corner Taker, Dead Ball Specialist, Crossing Threat, Aerial Threat, Box Presence, Set Piece Blocker) to surface dead-ball value a generic recruitment score would miss.

Hidden gems

Independent of Model Value entirely: every player's per-90 output is z-scored against their own position peers, and anyone with a standout z-score (≥1.8) on breadth and peak gets classified and ranked by anomaly score — catching statistical standouts the valuation model's market-value calibration might still underrate.
